questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University ranking and access to professors with international recognition for their research. Proximity to Denmark was also a small factor.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Also, when you spend the majority of your time at the university, it is preferable that the university has good facilities (well funded).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was really easy to come by and their administration continously sends you update regarding social events for incoming students and deadlines for, e.g., course registration etc. There is a check-list that covers most of the steps that need to be done before, during and after the exchange stay. This can be found on their website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There are events where the student association will answer question / show you around. The student exchange office is really helpfull, as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Campus housing was fairly easy to find. Just remember to apply for exchange student housing in time. Student housing is relatively close/far away from the university depending on your campus/courses.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Cost of public transport is fairly high, so try to not live outside the city, Zone (110).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process, courses, exams, etc., is really straight forward. You will recieve a link from the student exchange office with guides on how and when to register. Specifically, they have a portal 'myStudies' in which everything from scheduling, registration/derigistration is handled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Video guides, student exchange office and written material on the requirements for obtaining credits (taking courses) at the different departments depending on your study programme.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had no issues registrering for the classes, although there were some classes which were specific to the full masters programme, hence not available to exchange students. Make sure to read carefully which courses you are allowed to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can apply for more courses (credits) than you want/need to take and derigister after trying each course for 1-2 weeks. This is a really good opportunity to see if you actually like the course(s).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
There is a website where the students rate the courses on workload, exam difficulty and so forth. I would highly recommend checking it out to see what other students have to say.
https://n.ethz.ch/~lteufelbe/coursereview/

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 MA courses and 1 BA course. The level of the material was not much different from KU, in my experience. However, the course material seemed more 'predictable' in that it was clear from the beginning (in all but one of my courses), what the students needed to get out of the course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. Lectures and exercise classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Large Language Models
Rigorous Software Engineering
Big Data for Engineers
Computational Statistics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Big Data for Engineers (or Big Data, same lecturer), is really good. It is very well structured.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you live outside student housing you have to get 'vouchers' (stickers) that you put on your (official) trash bags to throw out. It costs about 15 DKK per trash bag. I also had to pay for radio license, electricity, gas, etc., seperately from the rent. In some cases you have to paint the room as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I knew it was expensive going to Switzerland, specifically Zurich. Nevertheless, food was quite more expensive than I would've imagined. Transport also relatively expensive, especially since I lived outside of the city zone. Eating at the school cafeteria can in some cases be cheaper than cooking at home. Protein shakes from COOP are a steal, highly recommend if you plan on working out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The student organization ASVZ has great offers for all types of sport activities!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The student association and adjacent association has all sorts of activities (hikes, tennis, dinners, etc.).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend going to Bern and take a boat down the Aaare River (starting point is in Thun). Also, go to Lucerne, it's a beautiful city. Obviously, go on some hikes as they are really accessible. If you are under 25, you can get really good discounts for train tickets (look up 'Half-fare' and adjacent offers on SBB).

Sign up for ASVZ and look at sports activity offers. Here you can meet a lot of local people as well who might share the same passion for a sport.

Besides the academic activities, it is really about making sure you see what Switzerland and Zurich has to offer; so go on a few hikes and meet some international as well as local students that you can do different things with, e.g., play sports, swim in the lake, etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Study, obviously.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Realy easy. It is similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the WhatsApp group and student associations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very nice and the streets are exeptionally clean.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing in time and start grant applications early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Note that many people go home in the study "break". That is, the exams can be as late as in August, so make sure you plan your summer accordingly with which courses/exams you take.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience a different student culture and taking course not available at KU.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a good balance between studying and having free time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
